title: Hakko FX-888DX Soldering Station Repair
subtitle: My Hakko FX-888DX fell off my desk and landed right on its port
description: After struggling to design and 3D print a custom support harness for the damaged port, I ultimately decided to replace the part entirely.

PXL_20260925_180415290.jpg: The FX-888DX is surprisingly heavy. When I accidentally knocked it off my desk, it took a direct hit face-down on its own port.
PXL_20260925_181759222.jpg: This is a brilliantly engineered product—neatly laid out and exceptionally easy to disassemble.
PXL_20260925_181947308.MACRO_FOCUS.jpg: This looks like it was chewed up and spat out.
PXL_20260926_094925554.jpg: My initial fix was to 3D print a support harness that wraps around the damaged port to lock it in place, using the existing motherboard screws as anchoring points. Navigating all the internal components meant a lot of trial and error, so I iterated the design in small increments.
PXL_20260926_094932286.jpg: I also designed a faceplate to hide the damage on the front. I used transparent filament just because it was already loaded in my printer, but I plan to reprint it in yellow once I'm sure the fit is dialed in.
PXL_20260926_101653442.MACRO_FOCUS.jpg: This is starting to come together nicely.
PXL_20260926_151822147.jpg: I happened to have yellow filament that was a really close color match to the Hakko faceplate.
PXL_20260926_161128593.jpg: The final design that I arrived at.
PXL_20260926_161128594.jpg: These are all of the incremental test and fit prints that I went through along the way.
Screenshot 2026-09-26 at 16.42.18.jpg: Eventually, I tracked down a replacement port featuring a threaded screw mounting system, which is much more reliable than my 3D-printed harness.
Screenshot 2026-09-26 at 17.04.11.jpg: The shipping cost (€11.99) is a real killer here. I hate paying more for delivery on a few grams of plastic than the actual item costs. I really wish companies would support hobbyists by shipping small parts like this via standard letter mail.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-30 at 21.29.41.jp: All wired up and ready to test.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-30 at 21.28.44.jp: It took a few days, but the replacement part eventually arrived.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-30 at 21.29.22.jp: Using my crappy old soldering iron to fix my beautiful new one. It took forever to heat up!
